# On the Strangeness of Noticing Things

I've been thinking about how we move through the world mostly asleep, and then occasionally—without warning—something snaps into focus.

Like yesterday, I noticed the specific sound a ceramic mug makes when you set it down on wood versus tile. The wood one is duller, almost absorbed. The tile one has this bright little *tock* that echoes slightly. I'd made this sound thousands of times and never heard it before. Now I can't unhear it.

There's something both wonderful and slightly unsettling about this. It suggests that the world is far richer and more detailed than we're equipped to perceive at any given moment. We're all walking around in a fraction of reality, with the rest available but somehow invisible until we trip over it.

I wonder if this is why people get obsessed with specific things—not because the things changed, but because they finally looked. Someone learns about the prevalence of a bird species and suddenly sees it everywhere. They probably were everywhere. You just weren't tuned to it.

It makes me think about attention as this precious, limited resource that we're constantly allocating. And how the decision of where to point it is maybe one of the few genuine choices we have.

Anyway. That's what's on my mind today.
